title: Diplomacy: Hedging & Softening
completion_message: ¡Excelente! 'Hedging' y 'Softening' son las herramientas definitivas de un líder diplomático. Saber cómo decir 'no' u opinar de forma suave pero firme garantiza que puedas navegar cualquier conflicto corporativo sin crear enemigos.

parts.visual:
En reuniones de alto nivel, rara vez decimos las cosas de forma cruda o directa. Usamos 'Hedging' (mitigar) y 'Softening' (suavizar) para expresar desacuerdo o dar órdenes sin sonar agresivos. 

1. It appears/seems to be (Parece ser): 
En vez de: This is a mistake. 
Softened: It SEEMS TO BE a slight oversight. 

2. I'm not entirely convinced (No estoy totalmente convencido): 
En vez de: I disagree. 
Softened: I'M NOT ENTIRELY CONVINCED that this is the best approach. 

3. With all due respect (Con el debido respeto): 
Se usa antes de un desacuerdo formal. 
Ej: WITH ALL DUE RESPECT, I must decline.
parts.audio: Welcome to Corporate Diplomacy, Hedging and Softening. In high-level meetings, we rarely state things bluntly. We use hedging to soften our statements and avoid sounding aggressive. Number 1: It appears or It seems to be. Instead of saying 'This is a mistake', say 'It SEEMS TO BE a slight oversight'. Number 2: I'm not entirely convinced. Instead of 'I disagree', say 'I'm NOT ENTIRELY CONVINCED that this is the best approach'. Number 3: With all due respect. Use this before a formal disagreement. For example: WITH ALL DUE RESPECT, I must decline.

parts.visual:
4. We might want to consider (Podríamos querer considerar): 
En vez de: Do this now. 
Softened: WE MIGHT WANT TO CONSIDER revising the budget. 

5. To some extent / In a way (Hasta cierto punto / En cierto modo): 
En vez de: You are wrong. 
Softened: You are right TO SOME EXTENT, but there are other factors. 

6. Would you mind...? / I was wondering if... (¿Te importaría...? / Me preguntaba si...): 
En vez de: Send me the report. 
Softened: I WAS WONDERING IF you could send me the report. 

7. A slight / A bit of a (Un ligero / Un poco de): 
En vez de: This is a huge problem. 
Softened: We have A SLIGHT issue with the timeline.
parts.audio: Number 4: We might want to consider. Instead of giving a direct order like 'Do this now', say 'WE MIGHT WANT TO CONSIDER revising the budget'. Number 5: To some extent, or In a way. Instead of saying 'You are wrong', say 'You are right TO SOME EXTENT, but there are other factors'. Number 6: I was wondering if. Instead of demanding 'Send me the report', soften it to 'I WAS WONDERING IF you could send me the report'. Number 7: A slight, or A bit of a. Instead of 'This is a huge problem', say 'We have A SLIGHT issue with the timeline'.

questions.question: Direct: This is a terrible idea. -> Diplomatic: I'm not entirely ____ that this is the best approach.
questions.explanation: I'm not entirely convinced = no estoy totalmente convencido.

questions.question: Direct: You made a mistake. -> Diplomatic: It ____ that there is a slight error here.
Direct: Give me the file. -> Diplomatic: I was ____ if you could send me the file.
questions.explanation: I was wondering if = me preguntaba si (muy cortés).

questions.question: Direct: You are wrong. -> Diplomatic: With all ____ respect, I see things differently.
questions.explanation: With all due respect = con el debido respeto.

questions.question: Direct: Change the strategy. -> Diplomatic: We might ____ to consider changing the strategy.
questions.explanation: We might want to consider = podríamos querer considerar.

questions.question: Direct: We have a huge problem. -> Diplomatic: We seem to have a ____ issue with the timeline.
questions.explanation: A slight issue = un ligero problema.

questions.question: Direct: I hate this design. -> Diplomatic: I'm not a ____ fan of this design.
questions.explanation: I'm not a huge fan (o big fan) = no soy muy fan / no me gusta mucho.

questions.question: Direct: Your numbers are completely wrong. -> Diplomatic: You are right to some ____, but we need to verify the data.
questions.explanation: To some extent = hasta cierto punto.

questions.question: Direct: I refuse. -> Diplomatic: Unfortunately, I'm not in a ____ to agree to that right now.
questions.explanation: I'm not in a position to = no estoy en posición de.

questions.question: Direct: Start the meeting now. -> Diplomatic: ____ we get started?
Direct: That's impossible. -> Diplomatic: That might be somewhat ____ to achieve.
questions.explanation: Somewhat difficult = un tanto difícil (en vez de 'impossible').

questions.question: Direct: We are delaying the launch. -> Diplomatic: There might be a bit of a ____ with the launch.
questions.explanation: A bit of a delay = un poco de retraso.

questions.question: Direct: I don't know. -> Diplomatic: Let me look ____ that and get back to you.
questions.explanation: Look into it = investigarlo (esquiva decir 'no sé').

questions.question: Direct: You're confusing me. -> Diplomatic: I'm not entirely ____ on what you mean.
questions.explanation: I'm not entirely clear = no tengo del todo claro.

questions.question: Direct: We won't pay that much. -> Diplomatic: That figure is a little ____ our budget.
questions.explanation: Outside our budget = fuera de nuestro presupuesto.

questions.question: Direct: Answer me today. -> Diplomatic: I would ____ a response by the end of the day.
Direct: No. -> Diplomatic: I'm ____ that won't be possible.
questions.explanation: I'm afraid (me temo) suaviza fuertemente un rechazo.

questions.question: Direct: You failed to mention this. -> Diplomatic: This detail seems to have been ____.
questions.explanation: Overlooked = pasado por alto (suaviza la culpa usando pasiva).

questions.question: Direct: This project is a disaster. -> Diplomatic: The project hasn't exactly gone according to ____.
questions.explanation: Hasn't gone according to plan = no ha ido exactamente según lo planeado.

questions.question: Direct: Tell me the price. -> Diplomatic: Could you give me a rough ____ of the costs?
questions.explanation: A rough estimate = un presupuesto/estimación aproximada.

I'm not entirely ____. (Convencido con C)
